scope: All 15 shipped heroes, Revolutionary War adult portrayals
user_approved_unknown_policy: Conservative provisional sizes, explicitly marked as estimates in this record.
method: One uniform scale and one ground inset per hero for all poses/directions/densities. Scale uses standing-equivalent body length, not image bounds. Manual anatomical calibration is approximate, especially under hats and in lunging/kneeling poses; it is not anthropometric proof. Keep the existing aspect ratio and build. Do not convert weight into an invented body width. No art samples cropped or redrawn.

heroes.name: Friedrich von Steuben
heroes.historical_finding: A 1994 Congressional tribute describes middle height; no verified numeric measurement located.
heroes.uncertainty: 69 in is a conservative provisional drawing value. A modern tribute is weaker evidence than a contemporary record.
heroes.build: Upright military bearing; no verified weight located.

sources.title: Congressional Record, September 12, 1994, p. 24364

calibration.note: Crown inferred under tall bicorne, not the top of the hat.

heroes.name: Benedict Arnold
heroes.historical_finding: J. L. Bell traces contemporary descriptions of middling or somewhat below middle height and muscular build.
heroes.uncertainty: 68 in is provisional. The often-repeated 5 ft 9 in militia record belongs to a different Benedict Arnold.

sources.title: Boston 1775: How Tall Was Benedict Arnold?

calibration.note: Deep lunge: estimated upright torso plus extended leg chain; sword and scarf excluded. Higher pose uncertainty.

heroes.name: Daniel Morgan
heroes.historical_finding: An early biography describes him as six feet; later accounts describe him as over six feet.
heroes.uncertainty: 72 in uses the conservative early description. Accounts disagree; do not present an exact Washington–Morgan ranking as proven.

sources.title: John Frost: Lives of the Heroes of the American Revolution, p. 89 (public-domain scan)
American Heritage: Daniel Morgan

heroes.name: Francis Marion
heroes.historical_finding: Historian Scott Kaufman distinguishes evidence of a slight figure from a later account of about five feet and 110 lb.
heroes.uncertainty: 61 in is an approximation of slightly over five feet, not a measured value. Later description has lower confidence.
heroes.build: Small and slight; much shorter than Washington is supported qualitatively.

sources.title: Age of Revolutions: Marion and the Historical Record
Christopher Miskimon: Francis Marion

calibration.note: Skull crown inferred beneath hat; slight forward lean allowed.

heroes.name: George Washington
heroes.historical_finding: About 6 ft 2 in, including ordinary shoes, in a later family recollection preserved by Mount Vernon.
heroes.uncertainty: Reported recollection; not a modern barefoot measurement.
heroes.build: Tall, powerful frame. 209 lb in the August 19, 1783 West Point weighing reported by NPS.

sources.title: Mount Vernon: Descriptions of George Washington, p. 122
NPS: Weight of a War

calibration.note: Upright; crown approximated beneath the hair mass.

heroes.name: Henry Knox
heroes.historical_finding: NPS says over six feet; this does not establish whether he was taller or shorter than Washington.
heroes.uncertainty: 73 in is a provisional drawing value, not an exact measurement; no reliable upper bound established.
heroes.build: Very heavy build; 280 lb at the same August 19, 1783 weighing. Retain broad torso; weight does not imply a measured shoulder width.

sources.title: NPS: Henry Knox
NPS: Weight of a War

calibration.note: Raised knee/stride shortens the vertical silhouette. Standing equivalent includes about 15 units of leg extension; retain the shared source ground line.

heroes.name: Horatio Gates
heroes.historical_finding: No verified height located; JAR traces problems in the later small, stooped caricature.
heroes.uncertainty: 69 in is a neutral provisional drawing value. Do not use the disputed caricature to make him exceptionally short.
heroes.build: Glasses are supported; exact body dimensions remain unknown.

sources.title: Journal of the American Revolution: The Myth of Granny Gates

calibration.note: Near upright; hair mass excluded from estimated skull crown.

heroes.name: John Glover
heroes.historical_finding: The Army Historical Foundation describes a short, stocky man; no reliable numeric measurement located.
heroes.uncertainty: 66 in is a provisional interpretation of short stature.

sources.title: Army Historical Foundation: John Glover
Journal of the American Revolution: John Glover

calibration.note: Crown under hat; oar and rope excluded.

heroes.name: Louis Duportail
heroes.historical_finding: No verified height or weight located in the consulted biography catalog and NPS portrait documentation.
heroes.uncertainty: 69 in is a neutral provisional drawing value. Portrait dimensions are not the sitter’s dimensions.
heroes.build: Existing build retained; no measured body width established.

sources.title: French Ministry of Defense: Duportail biography catalog
NPS: Peale portrait of Duportail

calibration.note: Kneeling: estimated crown-to-hip plus extended thigh/lower leg; divider and hat excluded. Higher pose uncertainty.

heroes.name: Mary Ludwig Hays
heroes.historical_finding: No verified height or weight located. Sources distinguish Mary Hays from the composite Molly Pitcher legend.
heroes.uncertainty: 65 in is a conservative provisional drawing value, not a recorded height or asserted population average.
heroes.build: Existing build retained; no measured body width established.

sources.title: National Women’s History Museum: Mary Ludwig Hays

calibration.note: Crown beneath cap; wide stance allowance; rammer and bucket excluded.

heroes.name: Nathanael Greene
heroes.historical_finding: World History Encyclopedia, citing David McCullough, describes him as nearly six feet.
heroes.uncertainty: 71.5 in is a drawing approximation of nearly six feet, not half-inch measurement precision.

sources.title: World History Encyclopedia: Nathanael Greene

calibration.note: Crown beneath hat; slight bent-leg stance allowance.

heroes.name: Israel Putnam
heroes.historical_finding: Richard M. Ketchum gives 5 ft 6 in in his American Heritage biography.
heroes.uncertainty: Reported secondary biographical height, not an inspected military measurement.

sources.title: American Heritage: Israel Putnam

calibration.note: Crown beneath hair; fur, raised weapon excluded.

heroes.name: Salem Poor
heroes.historical_finding: No verified height or weight located in the NPS biography or its Patriots of Color research.
heroes.uncertainty: 69 in is a neutral provisional drawing value. Not inferred from racial identity or modern commemorative artwork.
heroes.build: Existing build retained; bravery descriptions do not establish body measurements.

sources.title: NPS: Salem Poor, including George Quintal research

heroes.name: Thaddeus Kosciuszko
heroes.historical_finding: The Kosciuszko Mound Committee describes a slender man, not tall, with a slight frame.
heroes.uncertainty: 66 in is a provisional interpretation, not a verified measurement.
heroes.build: Slender and lightly built; no numeric weight or width established.

sources.title: Kosciuszko Mound Committee: Friend of Freedom, p. 44

calibration.note: Running stride: modest extended-leg allowance; shovel and map excluded. Higher pose uncertainty.

heroes.name: William Prescott
heroes.historical_finding: A retrospective battle account quoted by historian Phillip Greenwalt gives six feet two or three inches.
heroes.uncertainty: 74.5 in is the midpoint of a recollected range, not a half-inch measurement.

sources.title: Emerging Revolutionary War: William Prescott
Richard Frothingham: Centennial, Battle of Bunker Hill, p. 17

calibration.note: Hair crown estimate; spread stance adds about seven units to upright equivalent.
